title: Beef Stroganoff
subtitle: Strips of tender beef in a soured cream and mushroom sauce
excerpt: Thin strips of beef fillet or sirloin cooked quickly over high heat with mushrooms, onion, and a splash of brandy, finished in a richly flavoured soured cream sauce. A Russian classic.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef Stroganoff is a Russian dish first recorded in a nineteenth-century Russian cookbook, named in honour of the Stroganov family, Russian aristocrats of considerable wealth and influence. The original recipe was relatively simple: slices of beef in a soured-cream sauce. The dish spread internationally through Russian emigres in the early twentieth century and was simplified and adapted as it travelled: the brandy, Dijon mustard, and mushrooms that appear in most Western versions are later additions. Beef Stroganoff became enormously popular in the United States and Britain in the mid-twentieth century. The quality of the dish depends on two things: using a tender cut of beef (fillet or sirloin, not braising steak) and cooking the beef strips very quickly over very high heat so they stay pink and tender. The soured cream must not be allowed to boil once added to the pan as it will curdle.

recipeTools.notes: A large, wide, heavy frying pan.

content.text: Cook the beef strips in batches without crowding the pan: a crowded pan drops the temperature and steams the meat. Each batch takes only 1 to 2 minutes over very high heat to achieve a good sear while leaving the inside pink. Remove each batch before adding the next and return all the beef together at the very end, off the heat or over the lowest heat, to warm through in the sauce. Add the soured cream at the end and heat only until just warm: do not let it boil or it will curdle.

items.preparation: or sirloin; cut into 1 cm thick strips across the grain

content.text: Season the beef strips. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over the highest heat. Sear the beef in batches for 1 to 2 minutes until browned but still pink inside. Remove each batch and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium-high. Fry the mushrooms in the butter until golden, about 4 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the brandy and let it bubble for 30 seconds.

Add the stock, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 3 minutes. Reduce the heat to very low. Stir in the soured cream and warm gently without boiling. Return the beef and any resting juices to the pan. Stir and heat for 1 minute. Scatter with parsley. Serve with rice or buttered egg noodles.
